text: Why do two address systems — MAC and IP — both exist, when neither can be eliminated?
choices: MAC addressing is flat and needs no administration, which is right locally; IP addressing is hierarchical and aggregatable, which is required globally
MAC is for hardware and IP is for software
explanation: Flat addressing means plug in a device and it works with a unique address and no assignment — exactly the right trade for one building. It cannot be made to work globally because it cannot be summarised. ARP exists solely to reconcile the two.
